hints.title: Deep Copy Reference Preservation
hints.text: Cloning a linked list where nodes contain arbitrary random references requires mapping original node addresses to clone node addresses. Can interleaved duplicate nodes eliminate separate storage?

hints.title: Interleaved Node Duplication
hints.text: For each node curr in the list, insert a cloned node curr_copy immediately after curr. The list becomes A -> A_copy -> B -> B_copy -> C -> C_copy.

hints.title: Random Pointer Wiring and Unweaving
hints.text: Set curr.next.random = curr.random.next for every node with a non-null random pointer. Finally, separate the interleaved chain into original and cloned lists.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of nodes in the linked list (0 <= N <= 1000)
complexity.notes: Three linear passes over the list without requiring an auxiliary hash table for node mapping.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Maintaining an auxiliary hash map consumes O(N) auxiliary space, whereas interleaved cloning achieves optimal O(1) space.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Interleaving clones in the existing list temporarily doubles list length to avoid memory allocation for a lookup table.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Careful restoration of the original list structure during the unweaving pass.

solutions.approach: Three-pass interleaved node cloning and unweaving
